overall: The AG found the Brookfield Conservation Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by not announcing a recording and by discussing an unnoticed topic at its December 18, 2024 meeting, but not by approving inaccurate minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair did not announce at the December 18 meeting that the meeting was being recorded.
allegations.key_passage: The Commission does not dispute that Chair Meeker was aware of the recording; rather, it acknowledges the violation and promises that going forward it will be mindful of the requirement that recordings must be announced.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the commission discussed a topic at the December 18 meeting that was not on the notice posted 48 hours before.
allegations.key_passage: It was not; as a result the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law when it engaged in a discussion of the topic.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the commission approved inaccurate minutes of its September 19 meeting at the December 18 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes of the September 19 meeting, as approved at the December 18 Meeting, substantially comply with the Open Meeting Law’s accuracy requirement.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
